newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban recapture positions in central Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Taleban recapture positions in central Afghanistan.

text.p: Afghanistan's fundamentalist Islamic Taleban have recaptured a number of positions from the opposition alliance in central Afghanistan, a Taleban spokesman said on Monday.
Taleban information minister Amir Khan Mutaqi said the fighting took place in the Lolenj district in the Ghorband valley some 130 km (81 miles), northwest of the capital Kabul.
The Ghorband valley leads up to the strategic Shibber Pass, which lies across one of the main routes to the opposition-held north of Afghanistan.

"Yesterday they launched an attack in Lolenj district and captured some positions. The Islamic army (the Taleban) launched an operation early this morning and retook the captured territory." Mutaqi said.
Some weapons and ammunition had also been recaptured, he said.
There was no independent confirmation of the minister's comments.

Mutaqi denied reports carried on Iranian Radio of opposition gains in the eastern Afghan province of Kunar. He said the oppositon forces had been defeated and the entire province was under Taleban control.

"No part of Kunar is in opposition hands. In the course of an operation yesterday (Sunday) the remaining bands of opposition around the town of Asmar were crushed. There is no longer any danger from the opposition in Asmar." said Mutaqi.
The Iranian radio report, broadcast on Sunday night, said that forces opposed to the Taleban had surrounded the provincial capital Assadabad, south of Asmar.
Mutaqi added that Taleban forces had also shot down an opposition plane on the front line in the remote northwestern province of Badghis.
There has been no independent confirmation of the state of fighting in Kunar or Badghis.
The Taleban are fighting an opposition alliance comprised of forces of the ousted government, northern leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum and Shi'ite leader Karim Khalili.
Meanwhile, two Afghan factions battling the Taleban militia were fighting among themselves near a northern town, an Afghan news service said.

The Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) said forces loyal to former government commander Ahmad Shah Masood, northern Dostum and some Shi'ite Moslem commanders had attacked positions held by former prime minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar's Hezb-i-Islami party around the town of Baghlan.

It said the anti-Hekmatyar forces had seized nine military positions from a Hezb-i-Islami commander named Sayed Rahman in an assault launched on Sunday night. Rahman counter-attacked on Monday, recapturing five of the posts, AIP said.
The agency said a total of at least four fighters had been killed and nine wounded in the fighting but there was no breakdown on how much it had cost each side.
Heavy fighting continued in the Baghlan area, the agency added.
Masood, whose followers are mainly ethnic Tajiks, is an old rival of Hekmatyar and his mainly Pashtun Hezb-i-Islami.

Baghlan, nearly 200 km (125 miles) north of Kabul, is the capital of Baghlan province, one of about nine northern provinces in opposition hands. The Taleban, who captured Kabul in September, control the rest of the country.
